newsitem.title: SPAIN: Analysts say Unisource deal good for Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say Unisource deal good for Telefonica.

text.p: The European Commission's approval of an alliance between Telefonica and the Unisource alliance was positive for the Spanish telecommunications operator, analysts said on Monday.
The commission announced its decision last week after Spain promised to liberalise its telecommunications market on December 1, 1998.
Unisource groups telecoms operators Dutch PTT, Telia AB of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT with Telefonica.
"It is positive that the European Union has authorised the participation of Telefonica in Unisource," said an analyst at Ibersecurities.
He recalled Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga's recent warning that failure to obtain this agreement could send the company's share price down by 15 to 20 percent.
Telefonica is at a crucial stage ahead of the privatisation of the state's remaining 21 percent stake.
An analyst at Inverban singled out Unisource's planned joint venture with U.S. group AT&T as the most positive factor of the deal.
"A possible alliance with AT&T would open up for Telefonica the single most important market in the world," he said.

Analysts said one hurdle to the deal, apart from the timetable for liberalising the Spanish telecoms market, had been Telefonica's cable television venture with Sogecable, under investigation by the European Commission.
Telefonica last week announced it was pulling out of the Cablevision project. "For Telefonica participating in Unisource is much more important than Cablevision," said the Ibersecurities analyst.
Telefonica traded up 15 pesetas at 2,670 at 1510 GMT.
